clauses.reason: The order exempts Maurice C. Latta from compulsory retirement for age and fixes its own end in the sentence "hereby exempt the said Maurice C. Latta from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending October 31, 1940". The exemption therefore ran through October 31, 1940, and that date is recorded as the first end, inclusive; the exclusive reading (the exemption ends as October 31, 1940 begins) is the alternative, and it would put the end one day earlier. The ending is the order's own stated term and the acting instrument is EO 8256 itself. The only operative sentence is the quoted one; the recital states the finding that the public interest requires the exemption and commands nothing else. Later events recorded for this clause: EO 8497 of July 26, 1940 states "I hereby further exempt the said Maurice C. Latta from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending October 31, 1941"; it cites this order by number, grants a further exemption for a later period, and is recorded as a later event; it does not alter the period stated in this order. EO 8904 of September 22, 1941 states "I hereby further exempt the said Maurice C. Latta from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending October 31, 1942"; it cites this order by number, grants a further exemption for a later period, and is recorded as a later event; it does not alter the period stated in this order. EO 9238 of September 3, 1942 states "Maurice C. Latta, Executive Clerk, The White House Office, who has heretofore been exempted from compulsory retirement for age until October 31, 1942" and exempts him again without a stated period; it does not cite this order and refers to an exemption until October 31, 1942, the end date fixed by EO 8904, so it is a later event in the serial exemptions and not an end of this order. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 each further exemption is a later event with its own date and quotation and is not this order's end.

research_rationale:
EO 8256 (1939-09-20, Franklin D. Roosevelt), a one-person exemption from compulsory retirement for age. Text and identity: the held text is the American Presidency Project transcription (grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; standing note: original not yet held). Page check per jobs/claim-kit/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md: the APP page record with the same sha256 in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl (common-crawl capture) has the heading "Executive Order 8256—Exemption of Maurice C. Latta From Compulsory Retirement for Age", which names this order number, its date (1939-09-20) agrees with the held text, and its text_sha256 equals the held file's. I read the whole text: one recital and one operative sentence, so the clause inventory is the single whole-paragraph clause. The sentence "hereby exempt the said Maurice C. Latta from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending October 31, 1940" fixes the end of the exemption on October 31, 1940; that is the first end, with the exclusive reading disclosed. The packet's later-events search (Federal Register disposition notes of 6938 catalog records from 1937 onward, plus operative sentences in 17521 saved order texts) returned two hits, "See" cross-references to the later further-exemption orders EO 8497 and EO 8904. The packet's name search of held order texts for the person named in this order is also cited. Other leads and later events are discussed in the clause reason. No held source shows an earlier end (revocation, supersession, or an earlier separation or death of the employee), so none is claimed.
